identity.name: Scattered Spider Pre-Attack OSINT + Help-Desk Profiling Stitched to External Footprint — Vishing-Precursor Recon Correlation
identity.summary: OSINT profiling of key personnel (ASM external footprint) and a burst of repeated low-pressure help-desk account-recovery calls are joined on one org/identity within a window; TIM attributes the pattern to Muddled Libra. The stitched recon storyline precedes and predicts the downstream MFA-reset takeover, so the recon phase itself becomes the terminal early-warning detection.
identity.description: Unit 42's 2025 Global IR Report (Social Engineering Edition) documents Muddled Libra / Scattered Spider (UNC3944) running a repeatable pre-attack playbook: gather detailed personal data from sources like LinkedIn to build convincing personas that pass identity verification, then make repeated low-pressure calls to the help desk, each time impersonating a locked-out employee, until a time-sensitive request prompts an MFA reset and identity takeover. The report notes the group progressed from initial access to domain-admin rights in under 40 minutes without deploying malware, so the only reliable early warning is the reconnaissance-and-profiling precursor itself. This scenario models that precursor as an ASM-plane detection-QA exercise: Cortex ASM/Xpanse (a defensive exposure-management capability) surfaces the org's own external footprint that fuels the pretext (exposed key-personnel identity data, social-media personas, and the org's externally-exposed SaaS apps / CSP tenants / federated-IdP login portal), while the IdP audit stream shows a cluster of help-desk-mediated account-recovery / MFA-reset contacts targeting those same exposed identities. No single event is a known-bad IOC — an exposed LinkedIn persona is not malware and a help-desk password reset is routine — so the detection value is entirely in the CORRELATION: an XQL surfaces the ASM footprint exposure of privileged personnel, a BIOC surfaces Cortex ASM's discovery of the org's externally-exposed federated-identity surface, an XQL and an auto-tuned ABIOC key on the anomalous help-desk account-recovery cadence against the exposed personnel, a validation XQL matches the pattern to Muddled Libra tradecraft in threat_intel, and the terminal correlation rule (CR-ASM-0006) stitches ASM footprint exposure × help-desk profiling burst × TIM attribution on one target org within a 7-day window into a single 'identity-takeover precursor' incident the DC presents as the early warning that fires BEFORE the MFA-reset takeover, not after.

campaigns: Identity-driven social-engineering intrusions against enterprise help desks and federated identity (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ASM-006 — Scattered Spider pre-attack OSINT + help-desk profiling stitched to external footprint as a vishing-precursor early-warning correlation.

prerequisites.description: Cortex ASM/Xpanse discovering the target org's external footprint and an IdP audit source (Okta/Entra) ingested into XSIAM so help-desk account-recovery events reach the analytics engine.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'ASM external footprint + IdP audit ingestion required'

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE: emit only the reconnaissance FOOTPRINT of the Scattered Spider
# pre-attack playbook against an AUTHORISED target org. No real victim identity
# data is collected and no help desk is actually contacted — the scenario steps
# stage the ASM-footprint and IdP-recovery telemetry shapes for Cortex to stitch.
set -euo pipefail
ORG="${TARGET_ORG:-acme-corp}"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] SIM-ASM-006 OSINT profiling key personnel of ${ORG} (LinkedIn-sourced personas)"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] enumerating ${ORG} SaaS apps, CSP tenants, and federated IdP login portal"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] simulating repeated low-pressure help-desk account-recovery recon calls (distinct locked-out personas)"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] CR-ASM-0006 recon storyline staged — identity-takeover-precursor early warning"

input_variables.name: TARGET_ORG
input_variables.description: Authorised target organisation whose external footprint + help-desk recon footprint the scenario emits.

expected_artifacts.description: Cortex ASM/Xpanse findings exposing key-personnel identity data, social-media personas, and the federated-IdP login portal for the target org.
A burst of help-desk-mediated account-recovery / MFA-reset events in the IdP audit stream targeting the ASM-exposed personnel within a short window.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: eventtype in (user.account.unlock, user.mfa.factor.reset) and actor_type = help_desk_agent

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-ASM-006 cleanup complete (recon footprint only — no state changed).'

biocs.name: Cortex ASM Discovery of Externally-Exposed Federated-Identity and App/CSP Surface
biocs.description: Cortex ASM/Xpanse product capability: discovery of the target org's OWN externally-exposed SaaS applications, cloud-service-provider tenants, and federated-identity login portal — the public attack surface that supplies a vishing operator the pretext material (which IdP, which help desk). This is a defensive exposure-management finding over the org's public footprint, NOT attacker-attributed enumeration: ASM independently surfaces what is externally reachable. An org exposing three or more distinct federated-identity/app services publicly is the exposure signal that feeds the identity-takeover pretext. Every discovered service is a legitimate public endpoint, so this is a behavioural/exposure BIOC, not an IOC match.
biocs.logic:
dataset = asm_findings
| filter finding_category in ("federated_idp_portal", "saas_app_discovery", "csp_tenant_discovery")
| filter exposure_state = "externally_exposed"
| comp count_distinct(discovered_service) as exposed_services by target_org
| filter exposed_services >= 3
| sort desc exposed_services
| fields target_org, exposed_services

abiocs.name: Anomalous Inbound Account-Recovery Cadence on Externally-Exposed Personnel
abiocs.description: An auto-tuned behavioural deviation: help-desk-mediated account-recovery / MFA-reset events cluster against identities that Cortex ASM flagged as externally exposed, at a cadence that exceeds the learned per-identity help-desk-contact baseline. Muddled Libra makes repeated low-pressure calls, each time impersonating a locked-out employee, so the tell is a burst of recovery events on exposed privileged personnel — not any single reset, which is routine. The ABIOC anchors the deviation to the identity's learned recovery baseline plus the ASM exposure flag rather than to a known-bad value.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter eventtype in ("user.account.unlock", "user.mfa.factor.reset", "help_desk.account_recovery")
| filter target_user_exposure_flag = true
| comp count() as recovery_events by client_org, target_user, bin(_time, 30m)
| filter recovery_events >= 2
| sort desc recovery_events
| fields client_org, target_user, recovery_events
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-identity help-desk account-recovery baseline (rare, self-initiated) -> a burst of help-desk-mediated recovery events on identities ASM independently flagged as externally exposed, anchored to the exposure flag and the recovery cadence deviation.

xql_queries.name: ASM Key-Personnel External Footprint Exposure
xql_queries.query:
dataset = asm_findings
| filter finding_category in ("exposed_identity", "credential_exposure", "social_media_persona", "federated_idp_portal")
| filter asset_owner_privilege in ("privileged", "executive", "it_admin", "helpdesk")
| comp count() as exposed_findings by target_org, asset_owner_username, finding_category
| filter exposed_findings >= 1
| sort desc exposed_findings
| fields target_org, asset_owner_username, finding_category, exposed_findings

xql_queries.name: Help-Desk Account-Recovery Reconnaissance Burst
xql_queries.query:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter eventtype in ("user.account.unlock", "user.mfa.factor.reset", "system.sms.send_factor_verify_message", "help_desk.account_recovery")
| filter actor_type = "help_desk_agent"
| comp count() as recovery_contacts by client_org, target_user, bin(_time, 1h)
| filter recovery_contacts >= 4
| sort desc recovery_contacts
| fields client_org, target_user, recovery_contacts

xql_queries.name: TIM Attribution — Muddled Libra Recon Tradecraft Match
xql_queries.query:
dataset = threat_intel
| filter indicator_type in ("actor_ttp", "campaign_pattern")
| filter threat_actor in ("Muddled Libra", "Scattered Spider", "UNC3944")
| filter ttp_fingerprint in ("linkedin_persona_verification_bypass", "repeated_helpdesk_profiling", "mfa_reset_takeover_precursor")
| comp count() as attribution_hits by target_org, threat_actor
| filter attribution_hits >= 1
| fields target_org, threat_actor, attribution_hits

correlation_rules.name: Scattered Spider Pre-Attack Recon Storyline — ASM Footprint x Help-Desk Profiling x TIM Attribution
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(ASM Key-Personnel External Footprint Exposure) AND (BIOC(Cortex ASM Discovery of Externally-Exposed Federated-Identity and App/CSP Surface) OR XQL(Help-Desk Account-Recovery Reconnaissance Burst) OR ABIOC(Anomalous Inbound Account-Recovery Cadence on Externally-Exposed Personnel)) AND XQL(TIM Attribution Muddled Libra Recon Tradecraft Match) observed on the same target_org within a 7-day window — fuses the ASM external-footprint exposure of key personnel, the repeated low-pressure help-desk account-recovery reconnaissance, and the TIM Muddled Libra attribution into ONE early-warning identity-takeover-precursor incident. The stitched recon storyline precedes and predicts the downstream MFA-reset identity takeover, so the reconnaissance phase itself becomes the terminal early-warning detection that fires before the takeover, not after.

analytics_modules.module: Cortex XSIAM Analytics — cross-source correlation of ASM exposure findings with IdP account-recovery behaviour
analytics_modules.note: Backed by CR-ASM-0006, which stitches the ASM footprint XQL, the help-desk recovery burst, and the TIM attribution into one incident.

products.evidence_query: dataset = okta_sso | filter eventtype in ("user.account.unlock", "user.mfa.factor.reset") | filter actor_type = "help_desk_agent" and target_user_exposure_flag = true | comp count() as recovery_events by client_org, target_user | filter recovery_events >= 4

dataset = asm_findings | filter finding_category in ("exposed_identity", "social_media_persona", "federated_idp_portal") | filter asset_owner_privilege in ("privileged", "executive", "it_admin", "helpdesk") | comp count() as exposed_findings by target_org, asset_owner_username

dataset = threat_intel | filter threat_actor in ("Muddled Libra", "Scattered Spider", "UNC3944") | filter ttp_fingerprint in ("repeated_helpdesk_profiling", "mfa_reset_takeover_precursor") | comp count() as attribution_hits by target_org, threat_actor

threat_scenarios.name: Vishing-Precursor Early Warning — Recon Storyline Correlation via Cortex ASM + Analytics + TIM
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex stitches the pre-attack reconnaissance that Muddled Libra / Scattered Spider runs before an identity takeover — external-footprint exposure of key personnel, enumeration of the federated-identity surface, and a burst of help-desk account-recovery profiling — into one early-warning incident that fires before the MFA-reset takeover, giving the SOC time to act on the recon phase itself.

threat_steps.objective: Cortex ASM surfaces the external-footprint exposure of key personnel and the federated-identity/app/CSP enumeration that fuels the vishing pretext.
preconditions: Cortex ASM/Xpanse discovering the target org's external footprint.
steps: Run the OSINT key-personnel profiling and federated-identity-surface enumeration footprint.
Observe the ASM footprint-exposure XQL and the enumeration BIOC surface the exposed personnel and services.
success_criteria: XQL `ASM Key-Personnel External Footprint Exposure` returns the exposed privileged personnel.
BIOC `Cortex ASM Discovery of Externally-Exposed Federated-Identity and App/CSP Surface` fires on the >=3-service exposure finding.

threat_steps.objective: Cortex detects the anomalous help-desk account-recovery reconnaissance burst against the exposed personnel and TIM attributes it to Muddled Libra tradecraft.
preconditions: IdP audit source (Okta/Entra) ingested into XSIAM.
TIM feed carrying Muddled Libra / Scattered Spider TTP fingerprints.
steps: Emit the repeated low-pressure help-desk account-recovery recon burst against the ASM-exposed identities.
Observe the recovery-burst XQL and the ABIOC fire, and the TIM attribution XQL match Muddled Libra tradecraft.
success_criteria: XQL `Help-Desk Account-Recovery Reconnaissance Burst` fires on the multi-target recovery cluster.
ABIOC `Anomalous Inbound Account-Recovery Cadence on Externally-Exposed Personnel` fires on the cadence deviation.
XQL `TIM Attribution — Muddled Libra Recon Tradecraft Match` returns the Muddled Libra attribution.

threat_steps.objective: The terminal correlation stitches the recon storyline into a single identity-takeover-precursor incident that fires before the downstream MFA-reset takeover.
preconditions: TC-ASM-006A and TC-ASM-006B signals observed on the same target org within the correlation window.
steps: Let the ASM footprint exposure, help-desk recovery burst, and TIM attribution land on one target org within a 7-day window.
Observe CR-ASM-0006 raise one early-warning incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-ASM-0006` raises exactly one identity-takeover-precursor incident stitching ASM footprint x help-desk profiling x TIM attribution.
The incident is raised on the reconnaissance phase, before any MFA-reset takeover event.

preventive_controls: Enforce strict, out-of-band identity verification for any help-desk account-recovery or MFA-reset request (callback to a manager, physical token, or verified-device check) so a LinkedIn-built persona cannot pass verification by voice alone.
Apply conditional-access policies that flag and block sessions from unrecognised devices/locations, which the Unit 42 report shows halted a Muddled Libra escalation.
Reduce the external footprint of privileged personnel (limit exposed identity data, monitor social-media persona exposure via ASM) so the pretext material is scarce.
Train help-desk staff to recognise repeated low-pressure impersonation calls and time-pressure MFA-reset requests.
detection_engineering: Correlate ASM external-footprint exposure of privileged personnel with IdP help-desk account-recovery bursts on the same identity/org within a window — the recon storyline is the early warning, since no single event is malicious.
Let Cortex auto-tune an ABIOC on per-identity help-desk account-recovery cadence rather than hand-authoring a static threshold per user.
Enrich the correlation with TIM attribution so the recon pattern is tied to Muddled Libra / Scattered Spider tradecraft and prioritised ahead of the takeover.
